validity.recommendation: Treat as GEM/OPEC-only entity; do not promote any spec to 'high'. Strongly consider merging into the A47-Yanbu line (P1897) as a kilometer-post segment rather than a standalone Riyadh pipeline — see duplicate note.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: No independent source confirms a pipeline named 'AY-1 KP 943-Riyadh'. The gem.wiki page contains NO narrative — only a name plus two citations to the OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin (ASB 2012 p.75 / ASB 2013 p.79). url_verifier on the ASB2012 PDF returned 200 but the document does NOT contain the token 'pipeline'; the ASB2013 flipbook page is paywalled (402/403). Every web hit for the exact name resolves back to gem.wiki itself; targeted searches for 'AY-1', 'KP 943', '153 km', '48 inch Riyadh gas' surface no primary or third-party source. The name is plainly an internal Aramco engineering designation: 'AY-1' reads as 'A47–Yanbu line 1' and 'KP 943' as 'kilometer post 943' — i.e. a row machine-extracted from an OPEC pipeline-segments table, not an independently attested named asset. Verdict: GEM/OPEC-derived entity with no independent confirmation — possible artifact of tabular extraction.

WHAT IS CORROBORATED (context, not the entity): The broader physical corridor IS real and Aramco-owned. The Master Gas System (developed from 1975, operational 1982) 'crosses from Yanbu on the Red Sea to Shedgum and passes by Riyadh' and was built to deliver gas to central-region power stations (MEED 'Master Gas System' page, verified). The East-West corridor carries a 48-inch line alongside the 56-inch crude line and a parallel NGL line (Oxford Business Group, verified). So a 48-inch gas line passing Riyadh as part of the A47–Yanbu / MGS network is physically plausible — but that corroborates the SYSTEM, not this specific 153 km segment, its endpoints, or its standalone identity.

CLASSIFICATION caveat: recorded Fuel=Gas. The Abqaiq/A47–Yanbu 48-inch corridor is genuinely ambiguous in the literature — the same right-of-way carries a dry-gas line AND a parallel NGL line (GEM separately tracks 'Abqaiq-Yanbu NGL pipeline'). Since the MGS explicitly transmits processed gas to Riyadh-area power plants, dry-gas classification is defensible, but cannot be independently confirmed for THIS row.

Net: real corridor, but this specific named entity and all its specs (153 km, 48 in) trace only to GEM/OPEC — do not rubber-stamp.

validity.recommendation: Investigate merge into P1897 (A47-Yanbu Gas Pipeline). P1903 is very likely a kilometer-post sub-segment of the same A47→Yanbu 48-inch line, not an independent pipeline.
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE/RELABEL: P1903's GEM segment_name is literally 'Pump Station and A47/Yanbu', tying it to P1897 'A47-Yanbu Gas Pipeline' (966 km, dia 42/48/56, operating, Aramco). The name 'AY-1 KP 943' decodes as 'A47-Yanbu line 1, kilometer post 943' — a point ON the A47–Yanbu line, and 943 km falls within P1897's 966 km total length. P1903's 48-inch diameter is one of P1897's recorded diameters. The sibling roster rows reinforce the pattern (e.g. P1900 'UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916' references the same AY-1 line and another kilometer post). This strongly suggests OPEC's segment-level table was ingested as multiple GEM rows describing portions of one trunk line — P1903 being the Riyadh-ward tail/spur of the A47→Yanbu corridor. Recommend a human merge/relabel decision: either fold P1903 into P1897 (OtherEnglishNames + extended geometry) or explicitly document it as a distinct spur with its own evidence (which currently does not exist).

summary: P1903 is a GEM/OPEC-only entity (no independent confirmation of the named pipeline or its 153 km/48-in specs); likely a kilometer-post segment of the A47→Yanbu line (P1897) — staged existence + duplicate concerns; underlying MGS/East-West gas corridor and Aramco ownership corroborated, the specific entity is not.
